items.title: Found this sweet girl injured and starving in a ditch. Sweetest dog I've ever met.
items.text: Found this sweet girl injured and starving in a ditch. Sweetest dog I've ever met.

Me too. I just happened to notice her while I was on a walk. The picture doesn't show it, but she was thin and couldn't walk. She was covered in abrasions and puncture wounds. I thought her leg was broken but she actually has nerve damage.  We are doing rehab and I think it and a good diet are helping. I already have three dogs and can't adopt another but I also can't fathom giving her up. She is an angel.

I don't understand people who can cause pain and suffering. This baby wagged her tail when she saw me coming into the ditch and gave me kisses all the way home - after longterm neglect and abuse.  Dogs are the best.
She's getting the medical attention and love. My dogs are jealous of the frequent pill pockets she gets and the therapy, which right now is standing therapy and massage.
Madelyn.
She’s working on it!! She weighed 36 pounds the day I found her. She’s up to 43 already and has more to go. I have to carry her in and out and when she gets tired so I feel every ounce!
Me too. She suffered and starved for quite a while before she was thrown out like trash. Some people shouldn’t have animals.

Yes, she went for her first visit the day I found her. She only had a general checkup, X-rays, and wound care that day. We go back Thursday to reassess the leg ( amputation is an option I would rather avoid but it’s the way my vet thinks it will go. She will already bear a little weight while standing, so I’m continuing to believe therapy can work.  Once all the leg wounds heal, I’m going to try splinting the leg during therapy time. )  she still needs vaccinations, a heart worm test, and a pregnancy test/spay discussion. 

We live in Louisiana. There are so many pit bulls in the shelters here it’s heartbreaking. Most will adopt them to animal rescue groups only.  She will never go to a shelter no matter what.
I’m posting a new picture of Madelyn now which shows her true beauty. She will need a perfect home someday and I’m hoping her future family May see her here.
Thank you so much. The look of joy on her face when I picked her up that day made me fall instantly in love.

items.title: Madelyn, one week after the ditch rescue
items.text: Madelyn, one week after the ditch rescue

I found Madelyn in a ditch last week.  I live in the country and animals are often thrown away in the area.  When I saw her, she wagged her tail. She couldn’t stand and was covered in cuts.  She was so happy when I picked her up - she is the most gentle, sweetest angel ever.

I thought her leg was broken but xrays confirmed the doctors belief that she has nerve damage in her front leg. She does have feeling in her foot so I am trying therapy, right now standing therapy and massage. When her wounds heal, we will go on to splinting and water therapy.  I would rather avoid amputation but it’s a very real possibility.

She has to go back to the vet for shots, heart worm assessment, and a spay consult. My fear is that she is pregnant. I don’t know what the recommendation will be if she’s far along.  The number of unwanted dogs in our area that get euthanized is staggering. She’s estimated to be 2 - 3 years old.

I have three dogs, all geriatric, and will need to find the perfect home for Madelyn.  Please keep her in mind if you know of someone who needs the bestest girl in the whole world.

Edit:  she weighed 36 pounds when I found her which is probably 20 - 25 pounds below her ideal weight. She weighs 43 pounds now.
Louisiana, I’ve posted a better picture and description of Madelyn.
